messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Incident created: SEV2 — CI/CD pipelines failing to start. Root cause suspected: GitHub Actions API / Packages registry errors. See status.github.com link (updating).

sam: saw a spike of failed workflows ~10:03 UTC. All hosted runners return 502/503 when fetching actions or downloading artifacts. Builds can't pull private packages from github.pkg. Repro: `npm install @redwood/internal@latest` -> 503.

nina: confirming — we're blocked on hotfix build for auth token rotation (customers hitting 401s). No deploys until we build and push new image.

kevin: @sam can we switch to self-hosted runners in cloud? We have a pool in GCP that usually can run the job, but workflows are org-level and might still hit API for actions/checkout.

sam: quick tests — self-hosted runners start the job but fail at `actions/checkout` step with 502 when contacting api.github.com for commit refs. So not just hosted runners, some API endpoints are degraded.

dev-qa: got logs from a failed workflow:
```
Error: Request failed with status code 502
at createError (/workspace/node_modules/axios/lib/core/createError.js:16:15)
at settle (/workspace/node_modules/axios/lib/core/settle.js:17:12)
at IncomingMessage.handleStreamEnd (/workspace/node_modules/axios/lib/adapters/http.js:269:11)
``` 

support-lead: customer impact — several enterprise customers reported delayed deployments and 5xx errors on inference endpoints because the latest auth hotfix couldn't be deployed. CS queue has ~12 tickets referencing "deploy blocked" and "auth error persists".

oncall-2: mitigation options:
- Option A: Patch at runtime to accept older tokens for a short window (dangerous but buys time).
- Option B: Build artifacts locally and push container images directly to container registry, then trigger k8s deployment without GitHub Actions.
- Option C: Mirror private npm packages to internal registry and re-run builds once registry is seeded.

sam: I'm going with Option B + C in parallel.

kevin: steps I started:
1) Spun up a bastion runner (self-hosted) in our GCP project with repo SSH keys.
2) Cloned the app, ran `npm ci --offline` — fails because private packages still fetch from GitHub Packages.
3) Started a local npm proxy (Verdaccio) and beginning to mirror critical packages (redwood-auth, redwood-core) from the last-known tarballs we have in artifact storage.

nina: I'm preparing an image build doc for manual push:
```
# on bastion
git checkout hotfix/auth-rotate
docker build -t gcr.io/redwood-prod/service-auth:hotfix-1895 .
docker push gcr.io/redwood-prod/service-auth:hotfix-1895
kubectl set image deployment/auth service-auth=gcr.io/redwood-prod/service-auth:hotfix-1895 -n prod
``` 

sam: started pushing images. Docker push is succeeding (registry unaffected). Triggered rollout for the auth service to reduce 401s. Monitoring user-facing metrics.

dev-qa: note — some integration tests still rely on github.com artifact downloads (release tooling). Skipping non-critical steps to expedite.

incident-bot: :information_source: GitHub Status: PARTIAL OUTAGE — Actions and Packages affected. (link)

support-lead: customers impacted: internal metric shows 7% of requests to /v1/auth returned 401 in last 30m, now slowly dropping to 2% since we started manual rollout. Communicating to enterprise customers in A and B segments.

kevin: open ticket with GitHub support (PR #open: 78321). Raised priority and attached workflow logs.

nina: handoff in 15m — @oncall-2 will take next shift. Current state: manual image pushed, canary at 10% healthy, rolling out to 100% in progress. Verdaccio mirroring 20% complete for private packages; will continue.

oncall-2: acknowledged — taking over. I'll monitor rollout, re-run any blocked deploys once packages mirrored or GH recovers. If GH status doesn't change in 40m, escalate to infra leads for extended mitigation (we may need to run emergency config to accept fallback tokens).

sam: quick note for postmortem: timeline of dependency failure, why our deploy/runbook couldn't complete, and actions: add artifact caching for private packages in CI, add a documented emergency path for direct image push, and evaluate multi-registry package mirrors.

support-lead: I've drafted customer-facing status blurb and sent to comms for approval. Will update customers every 30m. :thumbsup:

kevin: thanks team. If GH resumes, we'll re-enable workflows to verify CI green and then decommission temporary runners. Otherwise continue manual deploys. Next update in 10m from @oncall-2.

oncall-2: logging final for my shift: canary healthy at 75%, auth 401s at 1.1%. Mirroring continued. Marking as active incident (SEV2)."
